title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers are using AI-generated deepfakes and voice clones to impersonate real people, including a South Florida immigration attorney, to defraud victims across Georgia and South Florida. The system being deployed is social media itself, which lacks verification that accounts belong to whom they claim. A human check, such as social platforms verifying professional credentials or flagging accounts impersonating licensed practitioners, could have reduced the scammers' ability to operate at scale.

This is impersonation enabled by generative AI. Criminals extracted voice and identity information from public sources and used AI tools to create convincing replicas that targeted vulnerable populations, specifically immigrants seeking legal services. What would have caught this is verification of identity at the point of service, either by the platforms hosting the impersonators or by potential victims confirming identity through independent channels before engaging.

It is not established whether the platforms were aware of the impersonation, whether they took action upon learning of it, or what technical measures they had in place to detect deepfakes and spoofed accounts.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfakes and voice clones for fraud schemes across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. Overall, the FBI received more than 1 million internet crime complaints totaling over $20 billion in losses.

Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia reported 71 complaints resulting in over $10.4 million in losses. Criminals use AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photos, and research personal relationships to make scams more believable. Common tactics include romance scams, fake investment opportunities, emergency requests, and grandparent scams. Experts recommend establishing code words with family members, verifying urgent requests through known phone numbers, and monitoring accounts closely rather than responding immediately to unexpected communications.
